items.text: BusinessToday (5 hours ago) confirmed: US President Donald Trump said that negotiations with Iran are advancing in a constructive manner. He also informed his negotiators not to rush into a deal, as time is on Washington's side. "The Blockade will remain in full force and effect until an agreement is reached, certified, and signed," he said. The "not rushing" language is a significant shift from "FAST or nothing left" (Day 80) and "very quickly" (Days 82-83). Trump now has leverage: Brent is falling (his approval ratings improving), Iran's economy is under pressure, and Iran's state media is claiming vessels are transiting (signalling Iran wants the deal too). "Time is on Washington's side" = Trump is comfortable waiting for Iran to make the remaining concessions on nuclear and tolls.

items.text: CNN live (1 hour ago) and BusinessToday (5 hours ago) confirmed: Trump and Netanyahu spoke on Saturday following reports of progress toward a US memorandum of understanding with Iran. Israeli concerns: a limited deal focused on extending the ceasefire and reopening Hormuz would fail to address Iran's nuclear program. Trump reassured Netanyahu he would "stand firm" — would not sign a final agreement without: (1) dismantling of Iran's nuclear enrichment sites, (2) removal of all enriched uranium from its territory. Netanyahu posted: "President Trump and I agreed that any final agreement with Iran must eliminate the nuclear danger. That means dismantling Iran's nuclear enrichment sites and removing its enriched nuclear material from its territory." This is the hardest nuclear condition yet — not just a moratorium, not just monitoring — full dismantlement + removal. Iran's position: keep uranium within the country. The nuclear gap has widened from Vance's 20-year moratorium to full dismantlement + removal.

assessment.body:
Monday 12:30 PM IST. Day 87. India's largest rally in weeks — and the nuclear gap widens.

THE MARKET PICTURE AT 12:30 PM
Sensex: +904 pts (+1.20%) to 76,319.48 at 11AM.
Nifty: +258 pts (+1.09%) to 23,974.95.
Nifty 24,000: 25 points away. The post-war normalisation trade is being priced.
Brent: $96-99 — below $100 for the first time in weeks.
Petrol/diesel hiked again — OMC Oil & Gas index +1.66%.
Auto best sector. PSU Bank, Banks, Financials outperforming. IT underperforming.
This is the rotation from defensive (IT) to cyclical (auto, bank, consumer).

THE TRUMP-NETANYAHU NUCLEAR CONDITION
Trump reassured Netanyahu on Saturday: the final deal will NOT be signed without:
→ Dismantling of Iran's nuclear enrichment sites
→ Removal of ALL enriched uranium from Iranian territory
Netanyahu posted this publicly — making it a formal Israeli condition.
Iran's IAEA-confirmed stockpile: 440.9 kg of 60%-enriched uranium.
Iran's stated position: keep uranium within the country.
The gap: Trump/Netanyahu demand full dismantlement + removal.
This is the widest statement of the nuclear gap of the 87-day war.
Yet Brent is at $96-99 and markets are rallying.
Markets are pricing the deal happening despite the gap — either Trump will soften the condition, or Iran will accept dismantlement.

TRUMP'S STRATEGIC POSITION
"Not rushing — time is on Washington's side."
Brent falling = US gas prices easing = Trump's approval improving.
Iran state media claiming 35 vessels transited = Iran needs the deal too.
Blockade stays until deal "reached, certified, and signed." No partial reopening.

EMKAY AND THE POST-WAR TRADE
"Market appears to be pricing in a post-war normalization in estimates and multiples."
Emkay: Nifty 29,000 March 2027 target.
FII sold Rs 2.13 lakh crore YTD — largest historical outflow year by May.
Reversal conditions: Brent $88-92 + rupee 93 + deal = structural FII return that could recover months of outflows in weeks.

THE SECOND PETROL/DIESEL HIKE
Announced Monday as Brent falls to $99.
The hike + falling Brent = OMC margin recovery inflection point.
At Brent $99 + hike: under-recovery reducing toward breakeven.
If Brent falls to $88-92: OMC losses eliminated.

VERDICT: Day 87 midday is India's best day since the ceasefire on April 8. The market is pricing a deal — Sensex +904, Nifty approaching 24,000, Brent below $100, auto and banking leading. But the Trump-Netanyahu nuclear condition — full dismantlement + removal of all enriched uranium — is the widest statement of the nuclear gap yet. Markets are betting Trump will soften it enough for a deal. If they are right: Nifty 29,000 by March 2027 is not a dream. If they are wrong: Day 87's +904 pts will be another false dawn in a war that has produced many.

featured.title: The Strait of Hormuz and the New Logic of Chokepoint Control
featured.desc: Chokepoint control is no longer binary (open/closed) but a layered spatial contest spanning seabed topology, island sovereignty, electronic warfare, and visibility asymmetry. The cartography of maritime control in the 2026 crisis.

featured.title: Geopolitics of LPG Supply in India
featured.desc: How India's LPG import dependency on the Gulf creates acute vulnerability during the West Asia War. Explores Hormuz exposure, alternative supply routes, and policy imperatives for energy security in a blockade scenario.

featured.title: Geopolitics of Fertiliser Supply in India
featured.desc: India imports 30%+ of its fertilisers via the Strait of Hormuz. This paper maps the supply chain risks to kharif and rabi crops, the strategic case for diversification, and what a prolonged blockade means for food security.
